subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw establish a permanent third-party AI-safety event API with manifest allowlisting, and if so should it be a host-bound attributed plugin API rather than the proposed optional service-context method and parallel SDK helper?
rationale: This choice defines a new public plugin and manifest contract, its security semantics, and who owns event provenance; code-level repair cannot safely choose that permanent boundary.

options.title: Redesign the attributed API
options.body: Keep the feature direction but bind emission to host-known plugin identity, normalized declarations, runtime schemas, and a single authoritative plugin API path.

options.title: Keep safety events internal
options.body: Land only the internal taxonomy and exporters for now, deferring third-party emission until concrete detector use cases establish the required contract.

recommendation.title: Redesign the attributed API
recommendation.body: Keep the feature direction but bind emission to host-known plugin identity, normalized declarations, runtime schemas, and a single authoritative plugin API path.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history connects this person to manifest normalization, service lifecycle, and plugin API boundaries affected by the decision.
